subclassFeature.name: Crimson Blade
entries: Your blood takes the shape of a crimson weapon, ready to reclaim the life you sacrificed.

As a Bonus Action, you create a blood blade in an empty hand or coat one weapon you are holding that deals Slashing or Piercing damage with your blood. You lose Hit Points equal to your Rogue level, but this loss cannot reduce you below 1 Hit Point. This loss cannot be reduced or prevented and does not trigger Reaper’s Harvest.

A created blood blade is a magical Melee weapon that deals 1d6 Slashing damage and has the Finesse, Light, and Thrown (range 20/60) properties. A coated weapon retains its normal damage and properties.
As a Bonus Action, you can return the weapon to an empty hand if you can see it within 60 feet and it is not being held by another creature.
This effect lasts for 1 minute and ends early if you use this feature again. When it ends, a created blade dissolves, while a coated weapon returns to normal.
While Crimson Blade is active, you gain the following benefits:

items: You have proficiency with the weapon.
Attacks made with the weapon count as magical for overcoming Resistance and Immunity to nonmagical attacks.
Whenever you hit a creature with the weapon, the attack deals extra Necrotic damage equal to a number of d4s equal to your Proficiency Bonus.

subclassFeature.name: Reaper’s Harvest
entries: Your crimson weapon steals vitality from the wounds it leaves, turning your enemies’ blood into borrowed life.

Once on each of your turns, when you damage a hostile creature with your Crimson Blade, you gain Blood Points equal to half the Hit Points it loses from that attack, rounded down. The creature cannot be a Construct, an Undead.
This amount includes all damage dealt as part of the attack but excludes damage exceeding the target’s remaining Hit Points.
As a Bonus Action, you can expend any number of Blood Points to restore an equal number of Hit Points to yourself or one willing creature you can see within 30 feet.

At the end of each of your turns, all remaining Blood Points are expended, and you regain an equal number of Hit Points. If this healing would exceed your Hit Point maximum, you gain Temporary Hit Points equal to the excess.

subclassFeature.name: Bloodstep
entries: You move with the swiftness of blood flowing from a fresh wound.
When you use a Bonus Action to expend Blood Points through Reaper’s Harvest, you can also take the Dash, Disengage, Dodge or Hide action as part of that same Bonus Action.

subclassFeature.name: Veinsever
entries: Once on each of your turns, when you hit a creature with your Crimson Blade and deal Sneak Attack damage to it, the creature cannot regain Hit Points until the start of your next turn, and it begins bleeding.

At the end of each of its turns, a bleeding creature's Hit Point maximum is reduced by an amount equal to 10 percent of its Hit Point maximum, rounded down (minimum reduction of 1 Hit Point). This reduction lasts until the creature finishes a Long Rest.

A bleeding creature can staunch the wound, ending the effect, by regaining any Hit Points or by using its action to succeed on a Wisdom (Medicine) check against your feature save DC. Another creature within 5 feet of it can use its action to make this check instead.

subclassFeature.name: Bloodmoon Ascension
entries: A spectral blood moon rises above you, and your body becomes a vessel for the life you have stolen.

As a Bonus Action, you transform for 1 minute. You can use this feature once, and you regain the ability to do so when you finish a Long Rest. The transformation ends early if you have the Incapacitated condition.
While transformed, when you damage an eligible creature with your Crimson Blade, you gain Blood Points equal to the Hit Points it loses from that damage, instead of half that amount.
You gain a Fly Speed equal to your Speed, and you can hover.

While transformed, the extra Necrotic damage from your Crimson Blade is replaced with Blood Loss. The target's current Hit Points and Hit Point maximum are each reduced by an amount equal to this damage. This reduction cannot be reduced or prevented, and it ignores Resistance and Immunity to damage. The reduction to the target's Hit Point maximum lasts until it finishes a Long Rest.
After you use a Bonus Action to expend Blood Points to restore Hit Points to yourself or another creature, you gain the Invisible condition until the start of your next turn.
